title: Test admin-route authorization via real route registration, not by unit-testing handlers
answers: How should I test that a route's permission/scope checks are correct?
How to test single-org vs multi-org authorization behavior for /api/admin routes?
Pattern for HTTP-level authorization tests in pkg/api
body:
Authorization behavior for /api/admin/* routes is verified with full HTTP-level tests that exercise the actual registered route and middleware chain, not by calling handler functions directly.
Pattern: build a webtest.Server via SetupAPITestServer with fake services (usertest.FakeUserService, orgtest.FakeOrgService, actest.FakeService, etc.), set hs.Cfg.RBAC.SingleOrganization to toggle single/multi-org, and inject an authntest.FakeService with separate per-org vs GlobalOrgID permission maps to simulate the caller having different permissions in org context vs global context.
See pkg/api/admin_users_test.go: setupAdminUsersAuthorizationServer and adminUsersAuthorizationCaller helpers, used by TestAdminUsersAuthorization_* tests.
Use this pattern when adding/changing authorization on any /api/admin/users (or similarly gated) route so single-org vs multi-org and scope-mismatch cases are covered end-to-end.
applies: pkg/api/admin_users_test.go and similar /api/admin route authorization tests
